notes.story: Publications desk item 17: Hurricane Helene raised microplastic deposition 3 to 22 times pre-storm levels across three western North Carolina mountain sites and delivered 18.8% of the year's deposition at Highlands Biological Station (Virginia Tech).
notes.journal: Integrated Environmental Assessment and Management, 25 September 2026, doi 10.1093/inteam/vjag130
caveats_on_screen: The '600 quadrillion' context line from the desk memo is deliberately NOT used; its date is unverified.
Cover says 'nearly one fifth', Virginia Tech's own wording.
Slide 6: three mountain sites in western North Carolina, one storm; 4.2% and 4.6% at the other two sites are shown so Highlands is not read as typical.
The per-site multipliers (22.7x, 8.1x, 3.4x) and the particle counts per square metre rest on a single outlet each and are not used.
Compare slide: the 'myth' is a common assumption, not a quote from anyone.
notes.fact_check: 2026-09-27 wave 2 GREEN: Integrated Environmental Assessment and Management, online 25 Sept 2026, DOI 10.1093/inteam/vjag130, PubMed 42554346. Lead author Austin Gray, Virginia Tech, with Western Carolina University, Highlands Biological Station and UNC. Deposition 3 to 22 times pre-storm levels across three western North Carolina sites; Helene = 18.8% of the year's deposition at Highlands, 4.2% Iron Duff, 4.6% Coweeta. Helene was Sept 2024; mountains, not the coast. Say 'nearly one-fifth'. Required wording applied.

caption:
Hurricane Helene (September 2024) raised microplastic deposition to 3 to 22 times pre-storm levels at three mountain sites in western North Carolina. At Highlands Biological Station one storm delivered 18.8% of the year's microplastics, nearly one fifth; 4.2% and 4.6% at the other two sites. Austin Gray, Virginia Tech, with Western Carolina University and UNC. Integrated Environmental Assessment and Management, 25 September 2026. Where does mountain plastic come from?

#microplastics #climate #pollution #science

slides.title: One storm. *Nearly one fifth* of a year's microplastic fallout.
slides.sub: Hurricane Helene at three mountain sites in western North Carolina. Virginia Tech, September 2026.

slides.title: Three mountain sites, *western North Carolina*
slides.body: Including Highlands Biological Station, where researchers measure how much microplastic is deposited across the year. The study covers before, during and after Hurricane Helene in September 2024.

slides.title: pre-storm microplastic deposition
slides.body: Across the three sites, Helene raised the deposition rate to between three and twenty-two times its pre-storm level.

slides.title: of the year's microplastics, in one storm, at Highlands
slides.body: Nearly one fifth of the site's annual microplastic deposition arrived with Helene.

slides.myth: Microplastics are deposited slowly and evenly through the year
slides.fact: One storm delivered nearly one fifth of the year's total at Highlands
slides.body: At one site, a single hurricane did nearly a fifth of a year's work.

slides.title: *4.2%* and *4.6%* of the year, from the same storm
slides.body: Iron Duff and Coweeta saw a smaller share. Three sites, one storm: this is the first US study of microplastic deposition before, during and after a hurricane, not a national average.
